title: Zunge mit Kräutern (Beef Tongue with Fine Herbs)
description: Prepared with beef tongue, chervil, and sorrel.

ingredients.name: peeled and tender cooked beef tongue

steps: Cut the peeled and tender cooked tongue into finger-thick slices
In a shallow saucepan, put 8 tablespoons butter with 1 tablespoon parsley, 5 sprigs tarragon, equal amount chervil, and some sorrel, all finely cut, and stir in the melted butter
Lay the cooked tongue slices in beside each other and cover with a butter-brushed piece of paper
10 minutes before serving, place the saucepan on the fire, remove the paper, let the tongue slices brown for 2 minutes on each side
Arrange them nicely in the center of a deep round bowl
To the herbs remaining in the saucepan, add juice of 1 lemon and some glaze dissolved in 1/8 liter soup, bring to a boil and pour this sauce over the tongue
Border the bowl with finely plucked parsley sprigs

title: Zungen in Fricandeau (Tongues Braised)
description: Prepared with tongues, chives, and turnips.
steps: Put the tongues in a pot with a bundle of parsley, chives, some yellow turnips, and salt, let cook until the skin can be removed.
Then lard them with finely cut bacon in three or four rows, one after another.
Arrange bacon, onion, yellow turnips, and ham all cut in thin slices in a casserole, place the tongues in it.
Fill with brown broth, cover the casserole, and let the tongues braise on gentle heat until tender enough.
Then remove them, strain the sauce, add two spoonfuls of good vinegar, and let the sauce cook until it becomes glace.
Then put the tongues back in, turn them on all sides until done. You can also lay a wreath of small braised onions around the edge of the dish.

title: Zweierlei-Kuchen (Two-Kind Cake)
description: A cake made with lemon, yeast, and cream.
steps: Mix 14 deca butter with 4 deca lemon sugar and 1 knife point salt
Add 3 deca fresh yeast dissolved in 1/8 liter warm cream and 40 deca flour
Stir well and beat the dough from the spoon until it releases from the spoon
Lightly mix in the stiff peaks of 3 egg whites
Roll out this dough on a flour-dusted board to finger thickness and cut out round discs the size of an ordinary plate
Press the dough in the middle with your fingers so that it forms a finger-wide and slightly raised rim
Cover these cakes and let them rise at a warm place until the dough has risen somewhat
Meanwhile prepare the following fillings: Cheese filling: 20 deca sifted curd is sweetened to taste and mixed well with 1/2 knife point finely cut lemon peel and finely cut toasted almonds

Poppy seed filling: 1/8 liter finely ground poppy seed and 1/2 deca vanilla sugar are placed in a saucepan, 1/8 liter boiling milk is poured in and stirred over the fire until it thickens, then mixed well with 1/2 knife point finely cut lemon peel as desired and 1 toasted spoonful

Form finger-thick strips on a flour-dusted board
Wrap these in wafers that have been moistened with water

Place over heat and cook while stirring constantly and rapidly into a thick preserves, being careful that the plums do not lose their beautiful color, which resembles that of apricot preserves.
After cooking for 10 to 15 minutes, fill hot into jars like the Apricot Preserves.
If desired, you can add 1 teaspoon of vanilla, cinnamon, or clove oil, or a mixture of these, while cooking the preserves.

description: Prepared with yeast, egg yolks, and plums.

ingredients.name: 3 ounces yeast dissolved in 1/8 liter cold milk

Stir in 1/2 liter flour and 3 ounces yeast dissolved in 1/8 liter cold milk until the dough releases from the spoon
Cover and let rest in a warm place until it rises by one-third

title: Zwiebärdt (Twisted Braid Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with egg yolks, yeast, and bacon fat.

ingredients.name: 3 Deca fresh yeast dissolved in 1/4 liter lukewarm milk

steps: Beat 12 Deca butter until creamy and add 8 Deca finely sifted sugar and 4 egg yolks one by one.
Stir in 3 Deca fresh yeast dissolved in 1/4 liter lukewarm milk along with 24 Deca flour and mix well.
Beat the dough until it separates from the spoon.
Place on a flour-dusted board, divide into five parts, and form two of these parts into finger-length, finger-thick rolls.
Place on a buttered baking sheet, cover, and let rise once more in a warm place.
Bake on the sheet in the oven at fairly strong heat until golden.
Remove from the sheet with a knife and cool on a board or sieve.

The next day, cut each roll lengthwise into two equal parts, place cut-side up on a dry sheet, brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with chopped pistachios mixed with coarsely cut almonds, and bake until light brown at low heat.

title: À la Braise (Braised Meat)
description: Prepared with ham, kidney, and bouillon.

ingredients.name: 3 pounds lean ham, cut into pieces
1 pound good kidney fat, cut into pieces

steps: Place the ham, kidney fat, bouillon, bay leaf, cloves, pepper, mace, onions, celery, yellow turnips, and parsley bundle on the fire
Cut the bacon into broad slices to cover the piece of meat or poultry to be prepared
Use a casserole with a very tight-fitting lid for the braise
Place glowing coals on top of the lid and beneath it so that it cooks as little as possible rapidly

title: A Baked Apple Pudding
description: A pudding made with apples, white sugar, and lemon.

ingredients.name: a quarter of a pound of white sugar

steps: Take nine large pippin apples
Pare and core them whole
Set them in the bottom of a large deep dish, and pour round them a very little water, just enough to keep them from burning
Put them into an oven, and let them bake about half an hour
Mix three table-spoonfuls of flour with a quart of milk, a quarter of a pound of white sugar, and a tea-spoonful of mixed spice
Beat seven eggs very light, and stir them gradually into the milk
Take out the dish of apples, which by this time should be half baked
Fill up the holes from whence you extracted the cores, with white sugar
Press down into each a slice of fresh lemon
Pour the batter round the apples
Put the dish again into the oven, and let it bake another half hour
Do not bake long enough for the apples to fall to pieces
Send it to table warm
Improve it by previously boiling in the milk a small handful of peach-leaves
Let it get cold before you stir in the eggs

title: A Baked Bread Pudding
description: A pudding made with bread, wine or brandy or rose water or lemon, and milk.

ingredients.name: a stale five cent loaf of bread
a quarter of a pound of butter
a quarter of a pound of sugar
a glass of wine and brandy mixed, or a glass of rose water, or the grated peel of a large lemon
a table-spoonful of mixed cinnamon and nutmeg powdered

steps: Take a stale five cent loaf of bread; cut off all the crust, and grate or rub the crumb as fine as possible.
Boil a quart of rich milk, and pour it hot over the bread.
Stir in a quarter of a pound of butter, and the same quantity of sugar, a glass of wine and brandy mixed, or a glass of rose water, or the grated peel of a large lemon.
Add a table-spoonful of mixed cinnamon and nutmeg powdered.
Stir the whole very well, cover it, and set it away for half an hour.
Let it cool.
Beat seven or eight eggs very light, and stir them gradually into the mixture after it is cold.
Butter a deep dish, and bake the pudding an hour.
Send it to table cool.

title: A Baked Indian Pudding
description: A pudding made with molasses, meal, and lemon.

ingredients.name: a quarter of a pound of butter
a pint of sifted Indian meal
a table-spoonful of mixed cinnamon and nutmeg
the grated peel of a lemon

steps: Cut up a quarter of a pound of butter in a pint of molasses, and warm them together till the butter is melted.
Boil a quart of milk; and while scalding hot, pour it slowly over a pint of sifted Indian meal.
Stir in the molasses and butter.
Cover it, and let it steep for an hour.
Take off the cover, and set the mixture to cool.
When it is cold, beat six eggs, and stir them gradually into it.
Add a table-spoonful of mixed cinnamon and nutmeg; and the grated peel of a lemon.
Stir the whole very hard.
Put it into a buttered dish, and bake it two hours.
Serve it up hot, and eat it with wine sauce, or with butter and molasses.

title: A Baked Plum Pudding
description: A pudding made with currants, raisins, and citron.

ingredients.name: half a pound of currants, picked, washed, and dried
half a pound of raisins, stoned and cut in half
a quarter of a pound of citron cut in large slips
two nutmegs beaten to a powder
a table-spoonful of mace and cinnamon powdered and mixed together

steps: Grate all the crumb of a stale six cent loaf
Boil a quart of rich milk, and pour it boiling hot over the grated bread
Cover it, and let it steep for an hour
Set it out to cool
Prepare half a pound of currants, picked, washed, and dried
Prepare half a pound of raisins, stoned and cut in half
Prepare a quarter of a pound of citron cut in large slips
Beat two nutmegs to a powder
Powder and mix a table-spoonful of mace and cinnamon together
Crush with a rolling-pin half a pound of sugar
Cut up half a pound of butter
When the bread and milk is uncovered to cool, mix with it the butter, sugar, spice and citron
Add a glass of brandy, and a glass of white wine
Beat eight eggs very light
When the milk is quite cold, stir them gradually into the mixture
Add, by degrees, the raisins and currants, which must be previously dredged with flour
Stir the whole very hard
Put it into a buttered dish, and bake it two hours
Send it to table warm, and eat it with wine sauce, or with wine and sugar only

title: A Beef-Steak Pie
description: A pastry dish made with beef, potato, and butter.

ingredients.name: two pounds of the best beef-steak, cut thin and well beaten
small bits of butter rolled in flour
mushrooms, or chopped clams or oysters (optional)
half a pint of cold water

steps: Make a good paste in the proportion of a pound of butter to two pounds of sifted flour.
Divide it in half, and line with one sheet of it the bottom and sides of a deep dish, which must first be well buttered.
Have ready two pounds of the best beef-steak, cut thin, and well beaten; the bone and fat being omitted.
Season it with pepper and salt.
Spread a layer of the steak at the bottom of the pie, and on it a layer of sliced potato, and a few small bits of butter rolled in flour.
Then another layer of meat, potato, &c., till the dish is full.
Add mushrooms, or chopped clams or oysters if desired, leaving out the hard parts.
If you use clams or oysters, moisten the other ingredients with a little of their liquor. If not, pour in, at the last, half a pint of cold water, or less if the pie is small.
Cover the pie with the other sheet of paste as a lid, and notch the edges handsomely, having reserved a little of the paste to make a flower or tulip to stick in the slit at the top.
Bake it in a quick oven an hour and a quarter, or longer, in proportion to its size.

description: Prepared with cream, yolks of eggs, and chocolate.

ingredients.name: a pint and a half of cream

steps: Boil over a slow fire a pint and a half of cream.
Have ready six yolks of eggs, beaten up with two table-spoonfuls of powdered arrow-root, or fine flour.
Stir this gradually into the boiling cream, taking care to have it perfectly smooth and free from lumps.
Allow ten minutes for the egg and cream to boil together.
Divide the mixture by putting it into two separate sauce-pans.
In one pan, mix six ounces of chocolate scraped fine, two ounces of powdered loaf-sugar, and a quarter of a pound of maccaroons, broken up.
When it has come to a hard boil, take it off, stir it well, pour it into a bowl, and set it away to cool.

For the other sauce-pan of cream and egg, blanch a dozen bitter almonds, and four ounces of shelled sweet almonds or pistachio nuts, and pound them in a mortar with rose-water to a smooth paste, and mix with an ounce of citron also pounded.
Add four ounces of powdered sugar.
To colour it green, add two large spoonfuls of spinach juice that has been strained through a sieve.
Stir this mixture into the other half of the cream, and let it come to a boil.
Put it aside to cool.
Cut a large sponge-cake into slices half an inch thick.
Spread one slice thickly with the chocolate cream, and cover another slice with the almond cream.
Do this alternately, piling them evenly on a china dish, till all the ingredients are used up.
Arrange it in the original form of the sponge-cake before it was cut, or in a pyramid.
Whip the whites of the six eggs to a stiff froth, and gradually mix in six ounces of powdered sugar, and twelve drops of oil of lemon.

Set it in a very slow oven till the outside becomes a light brown colour.

title: A Christmas Goose Pie
description: A pastry dish made with goose, fowl, and tongue.

ingredients.name: a pint and a half of water

steps: Put into a sauce-pan one pound of butter cut up, and a pint and a half of water; stir it while it is melting, and let it come to a boil.
Skim off whatever milk or impurity may rise to the top.
Have ready four pounds of flour sifted into a pan.
Make a hole in the middle of it, and pour in the melted butter while hot.

Mix it with a spoon to a stiff paste, adding the beaten yolks of three or four eggs, and then knead it very well with your hands, on the pasteboard, keeping it dredged with flour till it ceases to be sticky.
Set it away to cool.
Split a large goose, and a fowl down the back, loosen the flesh all over with a sharp knife, and take out all the bones.
Parboil a smoked tongue; peel it and cut off the root.
Mix together a powdered nutmeg, a quarter of an ounce of powdered mace, a tea-spoonful of pepper, and a tea-spoonful of salt, and season with them the fowl and the goose.
Roll out the paste near an inch thick, and divide it into three pieces.
Cut out two of them of an oval form for the top and bottom; and the other into a long straight piece for the sides or walls of the pie.
Brush the paste all over with beaten white of egg, and set on the bottom the piece that is to form the wall, pinching the edges together, and cementing them with white of egg.

Put in first the goose, then the fowl, and then the tongue.
Fill up what space is left with pieces of the flesh of pigeons, or of partridges, quails, or any game that is convenient.
Add some bits of ham, or some force-meat balls.
Cover the other ingredients with half a pound of butter, and put on the top crust, which must be of an oval form to correspond with the bottom.
Place the lid not quite on the top edge of the wall, but an inch and a half below it.
Close it very well, and ornament the sides and top with festoons and leaves cut out of paste.
Notch the edges handsomely, and put a paste flower in the centre.
Glaze the whole with beaten yolk of egg, and bind the pie all round with a double fold of white paper.

steps: The night before you make this pudding, take a piece of rennet, in size rather more than two inches square, and carefully wash off in two cold waters all the salt from the outside

description: Prepared with beef, onions or shalots, and marrow.

steps: Take the bone out of a round of fresh beef, and beat the meat well all over to make it tender.
Chop and mix together equal quantities of sweet marjoram and sweet basil, the leaves picked from the stalks and rubbed fine.
Chop also some small onions or shalots, and some parsley; the marrow from the bone of the beef; and a quarter of a pound, or more of suet.

Proportion the quantity of stuffing to the size of the round of beef.
Fasten it well with skewers, and tie it round firmly with a piece of tape, so as to keep it compact and in good shape.
It is best to prepare the meat the day before it is to be cooked.

Lay the beef upon them, and cover the top of the meat with more slices of ham.

Pour in from half a pint to a pint of water, and if convenient, add two calves' feet cut in half.
Cover the pan closely, set it in an oven and let it bake for at least six hours; or seven or eight, according to the size.
When it is thoroughly done, take out the beef and lay it on a dish with the vegetables round it.

steps: Mix together ten gallons of water, and ten gallons of the best West India molasses.

Then take out half the liquid, and put it into a tub.
Have ready eight bushels of fine sound apples, pared, cored and quartered.
Throw them gradually into the liquid that is still boiling on the fire.
Let it continue to boil hard, and as it thickens, add by degrees the other half of the molasses and water, (that which has been put into the tub.)
Stir it frequently to prevent its scorching, and to make it of equal consistence throughout.
Boil it ten or twelve hours, continuing to stir it.
At night take it out of the kettle, and set it in tubs to cool; covering it carefully.
Wash out the kettle and wipe it very dry.
Next morning boil the apple butter six or eight hours longer; it should boil eighteen hours altogether.
Then an hour before you take it finally out, stir in a pound of mixed spice cloves, mace, cinnamon, and nutmeg, all finely powdered.
When entirely done, put up the apple butter in stone or earthen jars.
